subject: Re: Lumine MVP deployment & SLOs — topology and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@lumine.ai>
Cc: Diego Alvarez <diego@lumine.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lumine MVP deployment & SLOs — topology and next steps

Hi Samira / Diego —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Short recap so we have a shared starting point and clear next steps. I attached a quick draft topology and the traffic matrix you shared.

Key customer goals (as we heard):
- Launch an initial MVP for the in-product summarization feature by mid-May (external beta)
- Target p95 generation latency <= 350ms for 512-token requests under expected load
- Average throughput target: ~60 concurrent requests during peak with warm KV cache
- Keep hosted costs predictable; prefer reserved/dedicated capacity if it materially lowers cost per token

Primary pain points you emphasized:
- Burstiness: nightly batch bursts plus day-time spikes from concurrent users (up to 3x baseline)
- Cold-start latency for first inference after scaling events
- Desire to avoid model-hosting complexity — prefer a managed path with an option to pin a supported private deployment later

Proposed technical approach (top-level):
- Start on Redwood Hosted using a dedicated pool (reserved) sized for expected peak with autoscale headroom for 2x bursts
- Model: 7B family (quantized), we proposed a Redwood-verified 7B-qat variant to meet latency/cost tradeoffs; fallback to a smaller 3B variant for extreme load to preserve availability
- Caching: prefix / KV cache for common prompts + persistent cache across requests to reduce token compute on warm flows
- SLOs: configure p50 target ~140ms, p95 <= 350ms, and a soft p99 alerting threshold at 600ms — early canary runs will validate these numbers

Open items we need from Lumine:
1) Confirmation of expected traffic distribution (attached mvp-traffic-matrix.csv) — Diego, can you confirm the % of short vs long requests and peak TPS?
2) A security contact and the procurement cadence if we need an NDA / MSA — contract team expects a person to loop in for redlines
3) Any must-have models or prompts that require custom tokenization or special pre/post-processing

Next steps / timeline:
- Today/Tomorrow: Lumine to confirm traffic matrix and provide procurement contact (Samira/Diego)
- Week of Mar 29: Redwood runs an internal sizing for a dedicated pool and shares a quote (attached redwood-quote-v1.pdf)
- Apr 5–9: Technical deep dive (1 hour) — focus on KV caching, warmup, and failover plan. Please confirm availability.

Attachments: lumine-topology-draft.pdf (high-level topology), mvp-traffic-matrix.csv (from Lumine), redwood-quote-v1.pdf

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi

From: Diego Alvarez <diego@lumine.ai>

Cc: Samira Khan <samira@lumine.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumine MVP deployment & SLOs — topology and next steps

Irene — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from ops side (see inline):

- Traffic distribution: short (<=128 tokens) ~65%, medium (129–512) ~28%, long (>512) ~7%. Peak concurrent users estimate is 180 active users which maps to ~70 concurrent inference requests in our load tests (we included the matrix in the CSV).
- Burst profile: we have a nightly aggregation batch (worker) that will fire between 01:00–03:00 PT and can add a sustained 1.8x baseline for ~30 minutes. During product announcements we could see up to 3x sustained for up to 10 minutes.
- Security/procurement: procurement lead is Maya Rao (maya@lumine.ai). I'll introduce her on the next thread.

Question for Redwood: can you size the dedicated pool to handle 2x the 70 concurrent requests for the default 7B recommendation and provide cost delta vs hosted autoscale? Also, any early suggestions for warmup strategy to reduce cold-starts for the nightly batch?

Forwarding our ops note with the sample payload sizes below for reference:

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Lumine sizing and configuration notes (do not externalize)

I ran a quick sizing pass using Diego's distribution and the Redwood 7B-qat profile. High level:
- Baseline concurrency: 70 -> recommend reserved pool for 140 concurrent capacity to cover the 2x burst target (keeps p95 headroom)
- GPU mix: 1x cluster of A100 80GB equiv nodes, or 2x H100 small nodes given their better throughput for quantized kernels (cost tradeoff: H100 provides ~1.6x throughput at ~1.4x cost)
- Warmup plan: persistent KV cache for hot prefixes + scheduled lightweight warmup calls 15 minutes before the nightly batches. Also propose a 2-minute rolling warmup after any scaling event.
- Degradation fallback: configure automatic routing to 3B-quantized variant when queue depth exceeds 180 requests; maintain consistent output by re-phrasing prompts if we hit the smaller model.

Action items for Irene / Marissa:
- Confirm we want us to propose both A100 and H100 cost options in the quote (I can size both and include hit rates).
- Align on a date for the technical deep dive (I suggested Apr 6 or Apr 8)
- I'll draft an SLO appendix describing alert thresholds and fallback policies to attach to the quote.

Quick note: the KV cache TTL will be a big lever for p95 — if Lumine can accept a 30–60s TTL for session prefixes we can reduce compute by ~22% in our sim.

-rishi
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

I'll also put the SLO appendix in the next quote iteration and share a short runbook for the warmup plan. If procurement prefers an initial 3-month reserved commitment to reduce unit cost we can include a trimmed discount in the next quote.
